subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 3: Musical Traditions of Ireland

promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How are the uilleann pipes supplied with air?
options: By a bellows pumped under the player's elbow
questions.explain: Unlike the Scottish Highland pipes, the uilleann pipes are bellows-blown, with the bellows worked by the elbow.

questions.q: What does the Irish word 'uilleann' mean?
questions.explain: 'Uilleann' means 'elbow', referring to the bellows worked by the player's elbow.

questions.q: The bodhran is played by striking the goatskin with a small double-ended wooden beater known as a:
questions.explain: The bodhran, a frame drum, is struck with a short wooden beater called a tipper or cipin.

questions.q: Which traditional Irish instrument is used as the national emblem of Ireland?
questions.explain: The Celtic harp is the official emblem of Ireland, appearing on coins and state documents.

questions.q: A standard (double) jig is usually written in which time signature?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance in compound duple time, notated as 6/8.

questions.q: A slip jig is normally written in which time signature?
questions.explain: The slip jig is in compound triple time and is notated as 9/8.

questions.q: In which time signature is a hornpipe usually written?
questions.explain: The hornpipe is in simple quadruple time (4/4), played at a moderate tempo with a swung, dotted feel.

questions.q: The term 'sean-nos' translates from Irish as:
questions.explain: 'Sean-nos' literally means 'old style' and describes a traditional form of solo singing.

questions.q: Which of these instruments produces sound WITHOUT using the player's breath?
questions.explain: The uilleann pipes are inflated by a bellows worked at the elbow, whereas the whistle and flute are blown directly.

questions.q: What is the main rhythmic difference between a hornpipe and a reel?
options: The hornpipe uses a dotted, swung rhythm while the reel uses even flowing quavers
The hornpipe is in 6/8 while the reel is in 9/8
The hornpipe is faster and the reel is slower
The reel is dotted while the hornpipe is even
questions.explain: Both are in simple time, but the hornpipe swings its quavers with a dotted feel, whereas the reel keeps them even.

questions.q: Which description best fits a reel?
options: A fast dance in simple time with continuous even quavers
A slow dance in compound triple time
A moderate dance with heavily dotted rhythms
A free-rhythm melody with no fixed pulse
questions.explain: The reel is a brisk dance in simple duple/quadruple time driven by a steady stream of even quavers.

questions.q: Describing a jig as being in 'compound duple' time means each bar has:
options: Two main beats, each divided into three
Three main beats, each divided into two
Four main beats, each divided into two
Two main beats, each divided into two
questions.explain: Compound duple time (6/8) has two dotted-crotchet beats, each subdivided into three quavers, giving the jig its lilting feel.

questions.q: Which combination of features is characteristic of sean-nos singing?
options: Unaccompanied solo voice, highly ornamented, sung in Irish
Choral harmony with instrumental backing, sung in English
Duet singing with fixed strict rhythm
questions.explain: Sean-nos is a solo, unaccompanied and richly ornamented style, traditionally sung in the Irish language.

questions.q: How is rhythm typically treated in sean-nos singing?
options: Free and flexible, without a strict regular pulse
Locked to a steady dance beat
Marked by a repeating drum pattern
Governed by a fixed metronome tempo
questions.explain: Sean-nos uses free rhythm (rubato), with the singer stretching and shaping the line rather than following a strict beat.

questions.q: The bodhran is best classified as which type of instrument?
questions.explain: The bodhran is a shallow frame drum with a goatskin head, providing rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: Because sean-nos is sung by one voice alone, its texture is:
questions.explain: A single unaccompanied melodic line with no harmony makes sean-nos monophonic in texture.

questions.q: You hear a lively tune with a bouncy, lilting 'diddly-dee' feel that fits naturally into groups of two dotted beats per bar. Which dance is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: The compound-duple lilt in groups of three quavers per beat is the hallmark of a jig in 6/8.

questions.q: A fast instrumental piece flows in continuous even quavers in 4/4 with no swing or dotting. Which dance form does this suggest?
questions.explain: Fast, even, unswung quavers in simple time are typical of a reel.

questions.q: A tune at a moderate tempo has a strongly dotted, 'swung' rhythm in 4/4 and finishes with three firm notes. Which dance is this?
questions.explain: The moderate tempo, swung dotted rhythm and characteristic three closing notes identify a hornpipe.

questions.q: A recording features a single voice with no instruments, elaborate ornamentation, a flexible free rhythm and words in Irish. Which vocal style is this?
questions.explain: An ornamented, free-rhythm, unaccompanied solo voice singing in Irish is the defining picture of sean-nos.
